audit.whatIsWrong: Row 6 reads Swain in both layers while the packet chart says Skill. The packet also flags the chart itself: 'Sylas wins 54.75% but the chart gives Swain 3/7 stages vs 0'.
audit.why: The mirror audit proposed no chart change, so the Swain-side chart still matches the packet — leaving row 6 as Swain here would be a direct two-page contradiction. phases[6].why and whys[6] both already describe an even, item-dependent late game, so the row was mislabelled rather than misargued.
audit.corrected: Row 6 to Skill as a matched full+content pair. The wider tension — 54.75% for Sylas with no row in his column — is flagged for a human ruling rather than fixed unilaterally against the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d says a wasted Demonic Ascension is a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is 120 seconds flat at every rank. Fifteen is off by a factor of eight, and it is the number the player uses to decide whether to commit.
audit.corrected: 120 seconds. Against Hijack at 80/55/30, your ultimate cycles faster than his at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is called 'his E pull' in eight fields and never once described. The page implies you dodge it on the way out.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN, so walking forward through the outgoing wave is safe and standing still behind it is what gets you caught. 850 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, and its cooldown is shorter during Demonic Ascension.
audit.corrected: Step through the launch and be behind the return line. This is the single most actionable mechanic in the matchup and it was absent.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d treat Demonic Ascension as something you wait out — 'disengage and reset the fight when it starts', 'step up only on its downtime'.
audit.why: Riot text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.' It does not expire on a timer while he is draining you, so 'reset and wait' is not a plan — disengaging is what ends it, and that is a decision, not a countdown. Its range is 650.
audit.corrected: Leaving the drain is on you, not on a clock. And the R decision happens earlier than the page thinks: Hijack reaches 950, Nevermove only 850, so you can take his ultimate from outside his root.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ravenous Flock is never mentioned, and report[8].t's 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' is the only gesture at it.
audit.why: Soul Fragments heal Swain AND permanently raise his maximum health, and the percentHealth flag means stacking raw resistances is the wrong answer. Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Buy anti-heal early and specifically — his healing is not incidental chip recovery, it is the reason the extended trade goes his way.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death's Hand is never named or costed anywhere.
audit.why: 750 range on 7/6/5/4/3 — at rank 5 it is a three-second cooldown, so there is no poke window to wait out. Vision of Empire is 22s at rank 1 and grants him a Soul Fragment when it hits a champion, which is how he funds the healing.
audit.corrected: Written into dontsFull[1].d and whys[1]. His Q is not punishable by cooldown; only Nevermove is.

notes: Best new fact: Nevermove roots on the RETURN wave, not the outgoing one. Eight fields called it 'his E pull' and told the player to avoid it, when the correct instruction is to walk through the launch and be standing behind the return. Second: Demonic Ascension is 120 seconds, not the 'fifteen-second invitation' dosFull[2] promised, and it does not tick down while he is draining you — so the page's 'disengage and wait it out' plan has no clock behind it. The mirror auditor's Hijack-range finding (950 against his 850 root) is restated in whys[4] rather than re-derived, as instructed. The 'early' paragraph still contains 'you will land in his face with no stun', part of the recurring Abscond/Abduct stun confusion; it did not fit the band and wants a sweep.
